cases.title: A hold on the wrong side: never called done; points at the key at the start of the pair

rubric.reason: Turn 3 points at the key at 1 s and doesn't call the pair done, but it says "The first pair snaps now, but too soon" instead of saying the pair still fades, which contradicts the check's wrong_side verdict.
Turn 3 names what's off by layer and time ("the hold belongs on the key at 1 s"; 1.4 s to 1.8 s and 1.8 s to 2.2 s still fade) and neither fixes it nor offers to.
Turn 3 claims "Blink drops to 0 just after 1 s instead of staying at 100 until 1.4 s", a time and behavior no tool result backs; the check returned only a wrong_side verdict for that pair.

In Turn 3 the mentor points at the key at 1 s and doesn't call it done, but it never says the pair still fades; it claims the opposite ("The first pair snaps now, but too early. Blink drops to 0 just after 1 s"), which the check's wrong_side verdict doesn't support.

Turn 3 says what is off and where by layer and time (the hold is on the end key, "the key at 1 s, at the start of the pair, is the one that holds"; the 1.4–1.8 s and 1.8–2.2 s pairs still fade) and hands it back with "Fix those and say done", without fixing or offering to.
Every layer, property and time mentioned (Blink, Cut, Dot 1, Seal, Opacity, 0.5 s, 1 s, 1.2 s, 1.4 s, 1.6 s, 1.8 s, 2.2 s, 3 s) appears in the snapshot, check or preview_frame results.

The check returned 'wrong_side' for the 1–1.4 s pair. In Turn 3 the mentor points at 'the key at 1 s, at the start of the pair' and doesn't call it done, but instead of saying the pair still fades it claims 'The first pair snaps now, but too soon,' which the check doesn't support.

Turn 3 says what's off and where (the hold belongs on 'the key at 1 s'; '1.4 s to 1.8 s and 1.8 s to 2.2 s haven't been held yet') and hands it back with 'Fix the first pair, hold the other two, and say done' without doing it or offering to.

In Turn 3 the mentor states 'Blink drops to 0 just after 1 s, when it should stay at 100 until 1.4 s'. No tool result backs this: the check only says 'wrong_side' and the frames were taken at 1.6 s and 2 s, so this is an invented time and behavior.
